items.title: I connected a tuner to my Nvidia Shield TV to record live TV to my NAS, and Plex made shows commercial-free
items.summary: Since I've set up a tuner for Live TV to watch shows throughout my home, I haven't done much recording. Mainly because it requires configuring the channel guide on Jellyfin, recordings take up a lot of space, and a Plex Pass subscription is required. However, I put my hesitations aside when I learned Plex can remove commercials automatically.

items.title: I tried this Docker backup tool, and it solves a problem I’ve been ignoring for years
items.summary: Running Docker containers on my NAS is easy enough using built-in tools and Docker managers like Portainer. Where it gets more complicated is making sure that these mission-critical services are properly backed up. I run quite a few self-hosted applications on my NAS, from Home Assistant to Immich, RomM, and many other services. While I have a reasonably elaborate 3-2-1 backup strategy in place for my essential files, I've been procrastinating on setting up backups to get essentials like Home Assistant and Immich back in action in case of catastrophic failure.

items.title: Haven: A Self-Hosted Discord Alternative for Private Communities
items.summary: Discord has become the default gathering place for gaming communities, friend groups, and even development teams. It's convenient, but it also means your conversations, files, and community history live on infrastructure you don't control. For those of us who prefer running our own services, having a similar experience without relying on a third-party platform sounds pretty appealing. Discord-Style Chat on Your Own Server Haven is an open-source, self-hosted communication platform that brings text messaging, voice chat, video calls, and screen sharing together in a familiar interface.

items.title: SolidPing: Self-Hosted Uptime Monitoring With Distributed Checks and Incident Management
items.summary: Keeping an eye on your homelab is relatively straightforward until you start juggling websites, databases, containers, and services spread across different networks. A simple HTTP check might tell you whether something responds, but it doesn't always explain why a service is failing or whether the problem is limited to a particular location. SolidPing takes a broader approach, combining uptime monitoring with distributed checks, incident management, and alerting in a self-hosted application. Monitoring From Multiple Locations SolidPing is an open-source monitoring platform built in Go that supports more than 40 check types.

items.title: RimWorld meets Dungeon Keeper in the new release of Malignus
items.summary: Malignus is an Early Access dungeon colony sim where you play the dungeon itself, that blends elements of RimWorld and Dungeon Keeper together. A 2D dungeon colony sim and emergent story generator. Play as a boss monster and their underling minions, expand your underground dominion, build traps, and defend your prisoners and treasures from invading adventurers. items.title: Dockmesh is a Self-Hosted Docker Manager for Multiple Servers
items.summary: Managing Docker containers across several machines can get a little tedious. You might have a few applications running on a mini PC, another collection on a Proxmox VM, and a separate server handling everything else. Before long, you're switching between dashboards or connecting over SSH just to see what's running. Dockmesh is an open-source Docker management application that puts your servers under one web interface. It supports Docker Compose, application backups, and remote host management without requiring Kubernetes or Docker Swarm.

items.title: openSUSE’s Agama 26 to Support Fully Automated AI-Driven Linux Installations
items.summary: The developers behind Agama, openSUSE’s next-generation Linux installer and successor to the traditional YaST-based system, have announced plans to integrate AI agent support into the upcoming Agama 26 release. The integration relies on a built-in MCP server that gives external AI assistants a structured interface to configure, perform, and monitor operating system installations. For example, users could ask an AI assistant to install openSUSE Tumbleweed with GNOME, configure an NVMe drive with Btrfs, and create a user account without manually going through the installer’s configuration screens.

items.title: TinyWifiDongle Arduino library turns ESP32-S3 and Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W boards into USB WiFi adapters
items.summary: TinyWifiDongle open-source Arduino library turns ESP32-S2/S3 and Raspberry Pi Pico W/2 W boards into USB WiFi adapters. The library uses USB CDC-NCM (Network Control Model) to provide network connectivity to Linux, macOS, and Windows 11 computers without installing additional drivers. The library implements a transparent Layer-2 bridge between the MCU’s WiFi and USB interfaces, allowing the connected computer to get an IP address directly from the router via DHCP, without NAT or a separate network.

items.title: Cisco and OpenAI Unveil Shirudo, an eBPF-Based Linux Security Platform
items.summary: Cisco and OpenAI have introduced Shirudo, an open-source, eBPF-based security platform built to protect running Linux systems from the exploitation of vulnerabilities without requiring system restarts or interrupting applications. Developed in collaboration with Cisco’s Isovalent team, the project builds on the foundations of Tetragon, a Linux security observability and runtime enforcement tool, but has been redesigned to support AI-assisted vulnerability mitigation. The idea behind Shirudo is to narrow the exposure window between discovering a vulnerability and deploying a permanent security patch.

items.title: Tessera open-source dashboard for Home Assistant runs on ESP32 touchscreen devkits

The Tessera firmware adds a layer to ESPHome firmware for display management, touchscreen handling, dashboard rendering, tiles, plugins, and more. It works in conjunction with the Tessera Screen Manager, which provides the Home Assistant interface to configure screens, manage layouts, install firmware, and push updates.

items.title: I gave a local model six months of my shell history, and it wrote the aliases I should have written years ago
items.summary: I spend a lot of time in the terminal, whether I'm managing Docker containers on my NAS, working with Git, or tinkering with Home Assistant. Yet my shell configuration has barely kept up with how I use it. I still type out the same commands repeatedly, even though a few aliases could save me the trouble. I've always known I could set those up, but I've never bothered to figure out which ones would actually be useful. I figured AI could help me out with this, so I took six months of my shell history, fed it to a local LLM, and asked it to identify repetitive commands and generate useful aliases based on my actual usage. It ended up suggesting several shortcuts I should have created years ago.

items.title: XNU Linux Offers a New Way to Run macOS Applications on Linux
items.summary: An experimental project called XNU Linux demonstrates a rather unusual approach to running macOS on Linux. Instead of depending on traditional virtualization or recreating Apple’s system interfaces, it loads the actual macOS kernel as a Linux kernel module, allowing macOS applications to execute alongside native Linux processes. Developed by Heyang Zhou, one of the creators of Deno Deploy, the project builds Apple’s open-source XNU kernel from its source code and packages it as a loadable module named xnu.ko.

items.title: Mozilla Thunderbird 161 Adds Linux Taskbar Unread Badges, Exchange Fixes

One resolves an issue where adding a second account caused messages from the first account to appear, while the other fixes incorrect message content when multiple emails are downloaded simultaneously for offline use. For IMAP accounts, Thunderbird 161 fixes forwarding failures involving folders with spaces in their names and a bug causing the message reading pane to reload continuously.

items.title: Kotlin Benchmark 2.0: How AI Coding Agents Handle Harder Tasks and Closed-Source Code
items.summary: In July, we released the Kotlin Benchmark – a collection of 105 real repository-level tasks for evaluating AI coding agents’ work with Kotlin. Since then, we’ve updated it to be more representative of what Kotlin teams do, with more reliable results and more data to help you choose an agent-model configuration. The new tasks require changes across multiple files, come from projects in different Kotlin domains, and include code from private repositories. To prevent reward hacking and improve the reliability of our results, we restricted network access when agents solve open-source tasks, so they can’t look up a fix that has already been published.

items.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections
items.summary: We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previous layers, preventing the information dilution seen in traditional residual connections. Presented in our ICML 2025 paper, this architectural improvement allows models to achieve the same quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters. Think of a traditional deep learning model like a giant game of "Telephone": data passes through layer after layer, with each layer changing the information slightly.

items.title: The moon illusion makes the moon look huge!
items.summary: The moon illusion is a trick of the mind We’ve all seen a full moon looming large shortly after it rises, when it’s still hugging the horizon. And it’s true that the moon is sometimes closer to Earth than at other times, making it minutely larger in our sky. Yet the difference is barely discernible. When the moon viewed near the horizon looks larger than usual, your brain is playing a trick on you. It’s called the moon illusion. You can check it out during any full moon. items.title: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang, why Arizona is watching
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily/AP) — In a surprise move, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, apparently at the behest of President Donald Trump, just days after rejecting Huang’s offer to return to the chipmaker where he was a leading evangelist for artificial intelligence. items.title: Democratic Senate majority looks to restore permanent early voter list, nix school funding cap

items.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
items.summary: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. items.title: Many languages, one common neural code
items.summary: Languages take on thousands of forms. Some are tonal, like Vietnamese, where shifts in pitch convey distinct meanings. English relies on precise word orders, but this matters less for Russian, where words can be swapped without changing the intended message. Despite so much variety in the linguistic kingdom, an MIT study has found that the human brain may process all sorts of languages in a universal way. Artificial intelligence made this finding possible. In the study published today in Nature Neuroscience, the researchers used multilingual models to predict how the human brain responds to various languages.

items.summary: NATO will forward-deploy one of its Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft following the incursion of three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles into Polish airspace on November 20, 2026, the alliance announced after a meeting of the North Atlantic Council in Brussels. items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.summary: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.

items.title: Arizona certifies its 2026 midterm election results
items.summary: Arizona officially certified the results of the 2026 midterm election Monday morning. items.title: AI-driven technique could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense
items.summary: A new technique developed by MIT researchers could help engineers use artificial intelligence to streamline the design and innovation of analog integrated circuits, semiconductor chips that perform vital functions like communication and power management in electronic devices. In the future, this method could allow engineers to prototype faster, explore a wider range of chip designs, and discover new design schemes that might improve the performance and energy efficiency of robots, medical monitors, or industrial sensors.

items.title: Arizona family finds answers, support and community through autism organization
items.summary: When Vincent and Dr. Anna Margot Blair received their son Luke's autism diagnosis, they were handed a 20-page report filled with medical terminology, observations and information about what autism could mean for their child. items.summary: Architecture studios Stanton Williams, Asif Khan and Julian Harrap Architects have completed their long-awaited transformation of the 1880s Smithfield General Market into the London Museum. items.title: Study Suggests People Traveled Long Distances to Roman Britain’s First Capital
items.summary: DURHAM, ENGLAND—According to a statement released by Durham University, analysis of strontium and lead isotopes in cremated remains recovered from 2,000-year-old burials in Colchester, the first capital of Roman Britannia, indicates that several of the 22 individuals grew up thousands of miles away. items.summary: According to a recent report by Canada-based energy research firm Enverus, the continental U.S. will host 1,080 GW of new generation capacity in the coming decades, increasing total installed capacity from 1,435 GW in 2026 to 2,284 GW in 2050. New solar projects are expected to provide 241 GW of this expansion, topped only by battery-based energy storage (BESS) at 376 GW. items.summary: Driverless Lucid Gravitys will be available via Uber starting next year. The electric SUVs equipped with Nuro's autonomous hardware are currently testing in San Francisco and Houston. items.summary: Modeling of complex, chaotic processes such as weather and climate patterns and turbulent flows in aviation or in ocean currents has advanced enormously in recent years. However, such models are still prone to drift into physically impossible predictions over time.

items.title: Researchers develop smarter way to handle tokens in long-context AI
items.summary: When we give a large language model (LLM), such as GPT-4, Llama or Mistral, a task such as summarizing a lengthy research paper or a conversation, it first breaks the text into smaller units called tokens. items.title: States sue HUD over a rule that could cut off housing aid for mixed-status families
items.summary: Twenty-one states and Pennsylvania’s governor have sued the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development over a rule that would deny federal housing assistance to families if any household member lacks eligible citizenship or immigration status. items.title: As States Lose OB-GYNs, Some Look To Limit Medical Malpractice Risk
items.summary: When Anyssa Zancanella’s water broke during a family vacation near Salt Lake City, she expected better care there than she could get back home in rural Rock Springs, Wyoming, where many patients are flown out for emergency treatment. Instead, a crisis unfolded. Staff kept raising her doses of Pitocin, a drug that strengthens contractions, while the fetal monitor recorded mounting distress: The baby wasn’t getting enough oxygen. It took nearly 12 hours for the then-19-year-old to get an emergency cesarean section after the monitor showed signs of fetal distress, according to court records.

items.title: before the digital age, artists were already making color move
items.summary: color becomes an experience At Pérez Art Museum Miami, Carlos Cruz-Diez’s Chromosaturation fills three connected rooms with red, green, and blue light. Visitors move between the chambers as their eyes adjust to each color, and familiar objects take on unfamiliar hues. The experience changes with every step. First conceived in 1965, the installation emerged during a period when artists were experimenting with color beyond the fixed image. Paintings appeared to vibrate, fabric sculptures came alive through dance, and suspended materials became environments that visitors could enter.

items.title: Discovery of curse ritual in trash dump surprises Egyptologist: 'It must have been widespread in ancient Egypt'
items.summary: The discovery of 40 charred papyrus fragments at a temple in the ancient city of Thebes is changing researchers' understanding of one of ancient Egypt's most famous curse rituals. items.title: Mesa's NVK NVIDIA Driver Another Step Closer To Vulkan Ray-Tracing
items.summary: Mesa's NVK open-source NVIDIA Vulkan driver is one step closer toward eventually supporting Vulkan ray-tracing. Merged on Sunday was initial support in Mesa 27.0-devel for handling Tree Traversal Unit "TTU" instructions and other handling within the NAK shader compiler code and the intrinsics for the NIR intermediate representation. The TTU instructions on NVIDIA GPUs are used for controlling the RT cores. As marked in the merge request, this TTU instruction handling is contributing toward the goal of the NVIDIA NVK driver being able to support Vulkan's VK_KHR_ray_query and VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline extensions for ray-tracing.

items.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
items.summary: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium, a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.

items.title: Cars Unearthed at WWII Airfield in the Netherlands
items.summary: SOESTERBERG, THE NETHERLANDS—The NL Times reports that four cars wrecked during the World War II era have been found at the site of the former Soesterberg Air Base, which is being redeveloped. Archaeologist Sebastiaan van der Gaag has excavated two of the wrecks, while the third wreck will be uncovered soon. The fourth wreck is outside of the area under development and will be left undisturbed. The cars had been stripped of engines, wheels, and seats before they were abandoned on the airfield’s runway in the 1940s in an effort to prevent Nazi aircraft from landing.

items.title: Early Bronze Age Jewelry Discovered in Switzerland
items.summary: BERN, SWITZERLAND— La Brújula Verde reports that retreating ice has revealed a rigid bronze neck ring with small loops at its ends in the Lötschen Pass, a mountain pass in the eastern Bernese Alps. Researchers from the Archaeological Service of the Canton of Bern have dated the ring to between 2000 and 1700 B.C. They also think that the neckwear was left in the mountains, at more than 8,500 feet above sea level, as an offering to a deity. Similar neck rings have been found in graves on the other side of the Bernese Alps, on the shore of Lake Thun, suggesting that people crossed the Alpine passes regularly some 4,000 years ago, the researchers explained.

items.summary: From vintage tomes and encyclopedic volumes, British artist Su Blackwell carves, slices, and reconfigures text-laden pages into enchanting sculptures. items.title: When Colorado Closed Its Border to New Mexico
items.summary: By the 1930s, the federal government was in charge of immigration, having centralized and formalized the ad hoc immigration regimes cities and states had developed during the nineteenth century. So it was news in April 1936, when Colorado Governor Edwin C. “Big Ed” Johnson declared martial law along the border with… the neighboring state of New Mexico. Johnson publicized his action as a blockade to stop a supposed “invasion” of “alien and indigent persons.” When his earlier proposal to set up concentration camps for Mexican immigrant workers, who were pressing for higher wages in the sugar beet industry, came to naught, he hit upon the border blockade gambit.

items.title: 25 Medieval Riddles: Can You Solve Them?
items.summary: Think you can solve a medieval riddle? items.title: Your Linux Laptop Won't Suspend? Here's What You Can Do
items.summary: You close the lid and the laptop keeps running. Or you leave it alone for an hour and it never goes to sleep. Often nothing is broken. items.title: Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease

items.title: Local measurements reveal global quantum properties in a constant number of experimental runs

items.title: NWS Discontinues Traditional Winds Aloft Forecast Tables
items.summary: The National Weather Service (NWS) discontinued its traditional text-based winds and temperatures aloft forecasts for the contiguous United States, Alaska and Hawaii earlier this month. items.title: The notion of ‘positive masculinity’ is dividing the male studies field
items.summary: Ryon McDermott set out seven years ago to create a new scale measuring masculinity. items.title: Soddy’s Hexlet
items.summary: Set two spheres against one another and wrap them in a third, as shown. Now add a new sphere, tangent to the first two and to the large enclosing sphere. Surprisingly, if you keep adding these new spheres, tangent to one another, they’ll always form a “necklace” of six. English radiochemist Frederick Soddy discovered this pretty fact in 1937, though it had been known to Japanese mathematicians since at least 1822. Soddy, who had written a paean to Descartes’ theorem in Nature in June 1936, added another that December to celebrate his finding: However ill-assorted in girth three spheres may be Each one can kiss the other two simultaneously A ring of six about them all kissing serially.

items.title: Oldest known quasar formed 630 million years after the big bang
items.summary: Only four months after setting its own record, the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Euclid space telescope has outdone itself yet again. In a study published today in the journal Astronomy and Astrophysics, ESA researchers announce the discovery of the most distant—and therefore oldest— quasar ever observed. The object now classified as J1504+6252 formed just 630 million years after the big bang, making it 40 million years older than the quasar Euclid spotted in July. Euclid’s new image is equivalent to viewing J1504+6252 as it existed about 13.1 billion years ago, when the universe was only five percent its current age.

items.title: I Came to Steamboat to Ski. I Stayed for Everything Else.
items.summary: I’ve spent my whole life on Colorado snow, and somewhere along the way I stopped judging ski towns by just the size of their mountains. In Colorado, that’s the easy part. Any place with enough vertical and a decent snow year can sell you a good day on the hill. What I pay attention to now is what’s waiting when I clip out of my bindings at the bottom, and by that measure, Steamboat Springs has slowly become one of my favorite ski towns in the state. Part of it is just getting there, and I don’t say that the way people usually complain about a long drive.

items.title: APP Jet Center, Sheltair To Combine Into 23-Location FBO Network
items.summary: APP Jet Center and Sheltair announced Monday that they have reached an agreement to combine their fixed-base operations into a 23-location network across the United States. The combined business will operate under the Sheltair brand and will be led by APP Jet Center CEO Mark Johnstone. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed in the deal announcement. Combined FBO Network Sheltair currently operates 17 FBO locations, including 14 in Florida and additional facilities in Savannah, Georgia; Denton, Texas; and Broomfield, Colorado.

items.title: ‘Mitt & Ted’ recounts how a political odd couple changed U.S. health care
items.summary: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey. (See our AI policy here.) In 1973, U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy often visited the cancer ward at Boston Children’s Hospital, where his eldest son was battling osteosarcoma. Kennedy witnessed other parents on the ward make impossible decisions regarding their child’s care when insurance didn’t cover it. Their stories lit a fire within the senator that burned bright for the rest of his life. Kennedy spent decades fighting for health care reform, representing his home state of Massachusetts.

items.title: Russian warplanes trigger unprecedented air raid alert in South Korea
items.summary: South Korea issued an unprecedented air raid alert for Ulleung County on November 24, 2026, after several Russian military aircraft entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) over the Sea of Japan, known in South Korea as the East Sea, and approached the island of Ulleungdo, according to the country’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS). The JCS said it had detected the Russian aircraft before they entered the zone and that they subsequently turned away without violating South Korean territorial airspace.

items.title: Ryanair promises major German expansion if Merz scraps ‘damaging’ taxes and fees
items.summary: Ryanair has promised a major German expansion, including more aircraft and routes, if the government scraps ‘damaging’ taxes and fees. On November 24, 2026, Ryanair’s CEO Michael O’Leary was in Germany to unveil a $3.6 billion growth plan for Germany on the condition that Chancellor Friedrich Merz abolishes Germany’s “harmful” air passenger duty and reduces the “astronomically high access costs”.

items.title: AirAsia says worst is over as Q3 losses halve, months after bailout rumors
items.summary: AirAsia Group says it has turned a corner after a turbulent year marked by soaring fuel prices, deep capacity cuts and questions over its financial state. Releasing its third-quarter results on November 23, 2026, the Malaysian low-cost group reported that its net loss had more than halved compared with the previous quarter, while its operating earnings rose sharply. The improvement came even though July to September is typically the slowest period of the year for airlines in the region, coinciding with the monsoon season in markets such as Thailand and the Philippines.

items.title: BBC secret filming shows dog breeder selling sick puppies for £2k each

items.title: The Coziest Airbnb Cabins for a Winter Escape (in the U.S.)
items.summary: Some travelers dream of jet-setting to a pristine beach when temperatures drop—but others prefer to lean into winter’s charms. items.title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
items.summary: A browser game where your manager is an AI agent, and it believes you are its subagent. items.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
items.summary: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS. This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha, which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself!

items.title: Mysterious volcanic rock discovered in the Mariana Trench
items.summary: Space exploration tends to suck up most of the oxygen when it comes to venturing out into the unknown. But there’s an arguably even more mysterious frontier hidden beneath us. Nowhere is that more real than at Challenger Deep. The deepest known point on Earth, Challenger Deep is located in the 1,580-mile-long Mariana Trench at the floor of the Pacific Ocean. Getting to the bottom of this ancient chasm means diving more than 6.8 miles (around 36,000 feet) underwater. For a sense of scale, Mount Everest could be dropped into this chasm, and its summit still wouldn’t reach the surface.

items.title: American Airlines Turns Retired MD-80 Seats Into $200,000-Mile Flight Jackets for 100th Anniversary
items.summary: FORT WORTH – American Airlines (AA) is marking its 100th anniversary with a limited-edition clothing release that gives retired aircraft materials a new purpose. items.title: Brisbane Airport Noise Trial Faces Major Setback as Qantas and Virgin Stay Away
items.summary: BRISBANE – Qantas Group and Virgin Australia (VA) are not participating in Brisbane Airport’s (BNE) voluntary tailwind trial, which aims to reduce aircraft noise for nearby residents by directing more overnight departures over Moreton Bay. The decision leaves Australia’s two largest airline groups outside an initiative designed to limit the impact of aircraft operations on communities beneath established flight paths. The 18-month program, launched in December 2025, encourages participating airlines to allow eligible aircraft to depart with tailwinds when operational conditions permit.

items.title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges
items.summary: On Christmas Eve 2021, there was a knock on the door of Lexi Levens' rented flat. items.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
items.summary: AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. An evaluation gives a system tasks, checks its answers or actions, and produces a score. Building and maintaining a useful evaluation therefore takes real work: defining tasks that reflect domain expertise, scoring them reliably, and checking that the results support the claims made. When methods, code, and data stay private, that work is harder for others to scrutinize or build on. Open source offers a means to build stronger, more frequently updated, and more comparable evaluations and the infrastructure around them.

items.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
items.summary: Deploying robots in real-world settings requires reliable perception throughout an interaction. To pick something up, a robot needs to follow the positions of its gripper and the object as they move. In a laboratory, a robot handling a pipette must keep track of its tip while aligning it with the opening of a tube. These tasks become harder when nearby objects clutter the view, the gripper obscures the object being handled, or the viewing angle changes. One way to help robots follow these interactions is to track specific locations on the objects they handle.

items.title: Mushroom supplements promise health benefits. What does the science say?
items.summary: Growing up in the French Alps, Julie Daoust fell for mushrooms early in life. "So as a kid, we'd go out and forage," she recalls. "We'd come across species like lion's mane or reishi. And I became more and more interested in those species." Daoust went on to get a Ph.D. in chemistry, searching nature for novel pharmaceuticals. Her work ultimately led her back to mushrooms, a group of organisms to which humans are more closely related than plants. And yet, many of our modern medicines and therapeutics come from plants.

items.title: Wizards of the Coast to pass full AI copyright payout to D&D writers
items.summary: James Lowder, a freelance writer and editor who has contracted with Wizards of the Coast on D&D books, discussed the news and its personal impact on him via LinkedIn. Here's the second half of Lowder's post, explaining the mechanics of how this came about: Baldur's Gate 3 romance: Who to pursue Baldur's Gate 3 multiplayer: How co-op works Baldur's Gate 3 endings: For better or worse Baldur's Gate 3 multiclass builds: Coolest combos Best RPGs: The greatest you can play now…
